## Purpose

This PR adds an opt-in FlyDSL FP8 path for MLA prefill attention on ROCm, following the approach of [ROCm/ATOM#2191](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/pull/2191). The target is Kimi-K3 on MI355X (gfx950).

It adds a new, opt-in MLA prefill backend, `ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8`, which subclasses `ROCM_AITER_FA`. Select it with `--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}'`; it is not in the ROCm auto-selection priorities. The backend:

- quantizes Q/K/V to FP8 with dynamic per-tensor scales and runs AITER's `flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_func` for the new tokens;
- keeps the new-token FP8 Q for the context chunks. Each chunk quantizes only its own K/V and calls the kernel non-causally with `return_lse=True`. The LSE layout (`[H, T]`, natural log) is unchanged, so `merge_attn_states` works as-is. The layer's softmax scale is passed directly.
- takes over context-free prefills too, in place of the ASM FP8 prefill (`mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd`). The metadata builder stops building ASM PS metadata when this backend is selected, and `AiterMLAImpl.forward_mha` then falls back to the common path.

Support is checked through the standard prefill-backend hooks. vLLM does not hard-code any shape or model:
- `supported_dtypes = [bf16]`, because the kernel writes BF16 output;
- `supports_compute_capability` requires gfx950;
- `is_available` requires AITER and the FlyDSL FP8 API;
- `validate_configuration` defers to AITER's `flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_supported` for the head dims.

An explicit selection that fails these checks raises at startup. At runtime, inputs the kernel cannot take (empty, or ≥2³¹ elements) use the parent's BF16 path.

`vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_per_tensor_fp8_quant.py` is a small Triton kernel adapted from ATOM#2191's fused QKV quantizer (MIT). It quantizes up to three strided `[tokens, heads, dim]` tensors in two launches, each with its own amax/descale. V is quantized directly from its strided view of the `kv_b_proj` output. Compile-time specialization does not depend on token counts (only the grid size does), so varying batch shapes do not recompile, and no atomics are used. Unlike ATOM's KV quantizer, element counts are runtime arguments.

**Why not reuse `ops.scaled_fp8_quant`.** vLLM's dynamic per-tensor quantizer (`dynamic_scaled_fp8_quant`, also behind `QuantFP8`) gives the same result: descales within 1e-6 relative, values within 1 e4m3 ulp. It is too slow for this path, for three reasons:
- It takes one 2D tensor per call, so Q/K/V need three calls (memset, amax, quant each).
- The strided V (row stride 256) takes its per-row path: one 256-thread block and one `atomicMax` per 128-element row, i.e. T×H rows.
- An all-zero input gets descale 0. ATOM uses a positive descale in that case to avoid FMHA NaNs, and this kernel does the same.

`rocm_aiter_ops.per_tensor_quant` returns wrong results for the strided V. GPU time on MI355X, 12 heads, q/k 192 and v 128 (v a strided view):

| Tokens | This kernel (Q/K/V, one call) | `scaled_fp8_quant` ×3 | `scaled_fp8_quant` ×3, V made contiguous first |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 50 µs | 189 µs | 59 µs |
| 8,192 | 50 µs | 1,318 µs | 237 µs |
| 65,536 | 352 µs | 10,165 µs | 1,306 µs |

At 65,536 tokens, V alone takes 9,284 µs with `scaled_fp8_quant` and 110 µs here. The existing op is faster only for a single small contiguous tensor (Q alone at 1,024 tokens: 21 µs vs 44 µs), which this path never quantizes.

**AITER requirement.** This needs an AITER build containing:
- ROCm/aiter#5718 (`flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_supported`)
- ROCm/aiter#5508 (short-query split-K)
- ROCm/aiter#5405 (`softmax_scale` in `flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_func`)

All three are already on AITER main. #5718 is the newest of them, so a build that has the capability check also has the other two. #5508 only affects performance. The current `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly (AITER 0.1.22.post1) predates them, so there this backend reports itself unavailable.

**AOT build.** ROCm/aiter#5796 and #5901 pre-compile the FlyDSL FP8 FMHA for Kimi-K3 TP8 (`12:12:192:128`, `varlen_cross` layout, 92 kernels) during AITER source builds, so serving no longer JIT-compiles them. The new-token call therefore passes `cross_seqlen=True`, as ATOM does.
- With `cross_seqlen=False`, the new-token call would use the `varlen` layout, which is not pre-compiled.
- For equal q/kv lengths, the two layouts give bit-identical output and LSE. Checked 8 batch shapes.
- Kernel time with `cross_seqlen=True` is within ±2% for most shapes and 7% faster for 1×8192. Batches of several equal-length sequences are slower: 4×2048 +15 µs, 8×1024 +4 µs.

Coverage check: the 92 AOT kernels (built with `aiter.aot.flydsl.fmha_fp8` from AITER main) were put into an empty `FLYDSL_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR`, and `FLYDSL_RUNTIME_RUN_ONLY=1` was set, which makes any cache miss raise.
- Through this backend, all 12 new-token and context-chunk calls were served from the AOT cache, and the cache did not grow. The calls covered 1–32 sequences, 17–8192 new tokens and contexts of 0–131072 tokens.
- With `cross_seqlen=False`, all 20 new-token calls missed.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs for FlyDSL/FP8 MLA prefill:
- #51551 (draft) adds a gfx942-only FP8 context-prefill path for 12-head Kimi-K3. It uses AITER's Gluon kernel (ROCm/aiter#4645) with static, offline-calibrated per-head scales. This PR targets gfx950 through FlyDSL, uses dynamic per-tensor scales with no calibration artifact, and also covers new tokens and context-free prefills.
- #53335 is a non-MLA FlyDSL BF16 attention backend.
- #58887 fixes an ASM PS-metadata race. It is orthogonal: that path is skipped while this backend is selected. Both PRs touch the `_fp8_prefill_enabled` gate in `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder.__init__`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to implement this change and to run the tests and benchmarks below.

## Test Plan

**Unit tests** (MI355X, gfx950):
```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k ROCM_AITER
python -m pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_flydsl_fp8_prefill.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_selector.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
python tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12 <changed vllm files>
```
`ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8` is added to `PREFILL_BACKENDS_TO_TEST` in `test_mla_backends.py`, so `test_backend_correctness` and `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` check it against the SDPA reference.
- GLM dims (v=256) are skipped at collection through `validate_configuration`.
- For this backend only, the tolerance is `rtol=2**-4, atol=0.3`. With per-tensor e4m3 Q/K/V, a row that attends to a few tokens is off by up to about 2⁻⁴·max|V|. The largest observed diff was about 0.25.
- A new `context_free_prefill` spec, run for this backend, covers the builder change that keeps `ROCM_AITER_MLA`'s ASM FP8 prefill from bypassing the selected prefill backend.

The registry and selector tests cover registration, bf16-only, gfx950 gating, availability, and deferring to AITER's check. The backend test file covers:
- the quant kernel against a torch reference: at most 1 e4m3 ulp, with strided V, empty and all-zero inputs;
- the backend's FP8 new-token and context-chunk outputs against its BF16 path, including short-q/long-kv chunks and sequences with empty context;
- FP8 Q reuse by the context chunk;
- `validate_configuration` rejecting a head dim that AITER does not support.

**End-to-end.** The server config is the InferenceX Kimi-K3 MI355X job (`kimik3_fp4_mi355x_mtp.sh`, conc 48, no spec decode). A/B differs only in the MLA prefill backend, and both runs use the same AITER build. The end-to-end numbers were measured with the first revision of this PR, which enabled the same code path through an env flag inside `ROCM_AITER_FA`. Apart from `cross_seqlen=True` (bit-identical outputs), the kernel calls are unchanged.

```bash
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --language-model-only --moe-backend auto --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL","max_cudagraph_capture_size":96,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"],"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[2,...,96]}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":224875000000,"lazy_offload":false}}'
# env: VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1
#      AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 AITER_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
#      VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_{A2A,Q_GATHER,KV_GATHER}=0
# FP8 arm: --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}'
```

- **Accuracy:**
  - lm-eval `gsm8k`, 5-shot, full 1319, via `local-completions`, `num_concurrent=64`, temperature 0.
  - InferenceX `kimi_tool_call_schema_full` (Kimi Vendor Verifier, 408 records, the CI eval for this job), run twice per arm.
- **Performance:**
  - InferenceX agentic replay: `aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp --concurrency 48 --benchmark-duration 3600 --warmup-grace-period 1800 --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126 ...`, the same command and aiperf commit as CI. One run per arm.
  - Prefill TTFT: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-output-len 1 --ignore-eos` at 8K, 32K, 128K and 64K-with-56K-shared-prefix inputs. A warmup pass runs first, and each arm is run twice.

## Test Result

**Unit tests** (MI355X, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`):
- `test_mla_backends.py -k ROCM_AITER`: 869 passed, 296 skipped. Three `ROCM_AITER_FA` cases (fp8 KV, scales 2/3, TP4) failed with CUDA OOM because another job had filled the shared GPU. All three pass when rerun individually, both on this branch and on `main`.
- All 290 `ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8` cases pass; the GLM-dim cases are skipped.
- Backend, selector and registry tests: 48 passed.
- `pre-commit` passes on the changed files. `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12` reports `Success: no issues found in 7 source files`.

**Accuracy (8×MI355X, TP8/DCP8):**

| Eval | Baseline | FlyDSL FP8 |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K 5-shot strict-match / flexible-extract | 0.9621 / 0.9621 | 0.9621 / 0.9621 |
| kimi_tool_call_schema_full, run 1 / run 2 | 0.9779 / 0.9877 | 0.9755 / 0.9951 |

The tool-call eval varies by about 2 points between runs of the same server. The two arms are within that noise.

**Agentic replay (InferenceX agentx-mvp, conc 48, 3600 s):**

| Metric | Baseline | FlyDSL FP8 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT p50 / p90 / p99 (ms) | 1176 / 3690 / 22443 | 1119 / 3106 / 16155 | -4.8% / -15.8% / -28.0% |
| ITL p50 / p90 / p99 (ms) | 51.1 / 74.6 / 188.0 | 49.2 / 68.2 / 130.5 | -3.8% / -8.7% / -30.6% |
| P90 interactivity (1000 / ITL p90, tok/s) | 13.40 | 14.67 | +9.5% |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 91,787 | 95,931 | +4.5% |
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 609.2 | 638.5 | +4.8% |
| Completed / errored requests | 2653 / 8 | 2744 / 6 | |

The errors are client-side aiperf `InvalidInferenceResultError`/`ClientOSError` records and appear in both arms. Neither server logged any errors. This workload has very long inputs (ISL p50 about 86K) and about 97% prefix-cache hits. Most prefill work is therefore short new-token segments against long cached context, which is where the FP8 kernel gains most. Shorter prefills also shorten the stalls of decodes batched with them, which lowers the ITL tail.

**Prefill TTFT (`vllm bench serve`, output_len 1, mean of 2 runs):**

| Case | Baseline mean TTFT | FlyDSL FP8 mean TTFT | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K fresh prefill ×128, c16 | 6676 ms | 6659 ms | -0.2% |
| 32K (chunked, with context) ×32, c4 | 5528 ms | 5441 ms | -1.6% |
| 128K ×8, c2 | 13252 ms | 12283 ms | -7.3% |
| 64K with a 56K shared cached prefix ×32, c4 | 5071 ms\* | 4758 ms | -6.2% |

\* Baseline run 2 only. Run 1 overlapped another client's load on the same server and was discarded.

**Backend micro-benchmark** (one GPU, 12 heads, qk 192 / v 128; FP8 times include quantization). The "context" rows time the new-token call plus one context-chunk call, with Q quantized once and reused, as in `forward_mha`:

| Shape | BF16 `flash_attn_varlen_func` | FlyDSL FP8 | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| new tokens 1×8192, causal | 313 µs | 229 µs | 1.37× |
| new q 8192 + context kv 64K | 3821 µs | 2469 µs | 1.55× |
| new q 1024 + context kv 64K | 1278 µs | 549 µs | 2.33× |
| new q 128 + context kv 64K | 1251 µs | 351 µs | 3.56× |

Short new-token-only calls (≤2K tokens) carry about 50 µs of host-side launch overhead from the quantizer. This did not show up end-to-end; the 8K fresh-prefill case is flat.

**JIT.** With an AITER build that includes the AOT kernels (#5796/#5901), the FlyDSL FMHA is not JIT-compiled while serving. Without them, each new FMHA configuration compiles on first use (about 1 s) and is then cached on disk. The Triton quantizer compiles 3 variants (Q/K/V, K/V, Q) once, which Triton caches.

3. **Default for FP8 KV.** Agreed, this should stay opt-in until there is a broader sweep. It also overlaps with your #44544 (`ROCM_AITER_ASM` as the gfx950 default for FP8 KV). I think the two can coexist as separate backends:
   - `ROCM_AITER_ASM` consumes the FP8 KV cache directly.

Three technical suggestions:

1. The quantizer grid uses the largest tensor size. V is smaller, so masked threads can still form out-of-range pointers. Please clamp indices or use separate grids.

2. The quantizer allocates temporary buffers on every call. Reusing fixed buffers could reduce the ~50 µs overhead for short inputs.

3. Please disable the ASM FP8 prefill path directly when this backend is selected, instead of relying only on missing metadata to bypass it.

Keeping this opt-in makes sense: short prefills show little benefit, while FP8 accuracy needs a wider long-context evaluation.

@ChuanLi1101 Thanks for the careful read — points 1 and 3 are fixed in 19a77e3, and I have numbers for point 2.

**1. Out-of-range pointers in the shared quant grid**

You're right that the grid is sized for the largest input, so programs can land past the end of a smaller one. Every load and store was already masked and the offset math is int64, so nothing was dereferenced or wrapped — but those programs still computed addresses they had no business computing. Both kernels now stop before that:

- `_partial_amax` derives its trip count per program, `tl.cdiv(N - start, PARTS * BLOCK)`, which is 0 once the program's stripe starts past the end of this input. It still stores its (zero) partial, which the reduce needs.
- `_quant` guards the body with `if start < N or start == 0`. Program 0 stays alive unconditionally so an empty input still gets its descale written.

I added `test_fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant_covers_every_element` to the kernel test: it plants the global max at `{0, BLOCK-1, BLOCK, STRIPE-1, STRIPE, numel-1}` for sizes straddling the 4096-element block and 1048576-element stripe boundaries, up to 3,145,735 elements. It fails if a single element is dropped (verified by shrinking the amax loop to one stripe). The change is perf-neutral: host 46.3–46.8 µs, e2e 349.2 µs at 65K tokens, same as before.

**2. Per-call temporary buffers**

I measured this on MI355X before changing it, since the buffers are tiny (`partial` is 3×256 f32, `scales` is 3 f32). Host cost of `fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant(q, k, v)`:

| Variant | Host | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|
| current (5 allocations) | 46.6 µs | — |
| reuse `partial` only | 44.2 µs | −2.4 µs |
| reuse `partial` + `scales` | 42.7 µs | −3.9 µs |
| one merged scratch allocation | 46.7 µs | +0.1 µs |

Where the 46.6 µs goes: 28 µs is the two Triton launches (an empty kernel with the same signature already costs 15.2 µs), 10.2 µs is `torch.empty` ×5, and the rest is the Python wrapper. So the ceiling on reuse is ~8% of host cost and ~1% of the 349 µs e2e at 65K tokens. The three FP8 outputs can't be reused at all — they are returned and stay live for the whole attention call.

Reusing `scales` specifically has a correctness trap: the backend keeps `self._q_fp8 = (q, q_fp8, q_descale)` across the forward, where `q_descale` is a view into that call's `scales`, and each context chunk then calls the quantizer again for its own K/V. A shared per-instance `scales` would be overwritten under the still-live `q_descale` unless keyed by tensor count — exactly the kind of implicit invariant that breaks later.

Given ~2 µs for the only unambiguously safe part (`partial`, which never escapes the function) against making a pure function stateful, I left it as is. Happy to add the `partial` cache if you'd still prefer it — it's a five-line change.

**3. Disabling the ASM FP8 prefill directly**

Agreed, keying off absent PS metadata was too indirect. There's now a single predicate in `rocm_aiter_mla.py`:

```python
def _asm_fp8_prefill_superseded(prefill_backend: object) -> bool:
    return isinstance(prefill_backend, AiterFlyDSLFP8PrefillBackend)
```

used in both places so they can't drift:

- `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder.__init__` folds it into `_fp8_prefill_enabled`, so the PS workspace buffers aren't allocated either.
- `AiterMLAImpl.forward_mha` checks the actual `prefill_metadata.prefill_backend` instance and defers to the parent, instead of inferring it from `fp8_prefill_qo_indptr is None`.

`test_mla_backends.py::test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` covers this through the `context_free_prefill` spec.

**4. Opt-in**

Agreed — it stays out of the ROCm auto-selection priorities and is only reachable via `--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}'`.

Yes. `forward_mha` passes `out` only together with `output_scale`, i.e. fused quantized output. That requires `supports_quant_output()`, which this backend doesn't claim (neither does `ROCM_AITER_FA`), so `out` is always `None` here and FlyDSL allocates the output itself.

This PR adds an opt-in FlyDSL FP8 path for MLA prefill attention on ROCm, following the approach of [ROCm/ATOM#2191](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/pull/2191). The target is Kimi-K3 on MI355X (gfx950).

It adds a new, opt-in MLA prefill backend, `ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8`, which subclasses `ROCM_AITER_FA`. Select it with `--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}'`; it is not in the ROCm auto-selection priorities. The backend:

- quantizes Q/K/V to FP8 with dynamic per-tensor scales and runs AITER's `flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_func` for the new tokens;
- keeps the new-token FP8 Q for the context chunks. Each chunk quantizes only its own K/V and calls the kernel non-causally with `return_lse=True`. The LSE layout (`[H, T]`, natural log) is unchanged, so `merge_attn_states` works as-is. The layer's softmax scale is passed directly.
- takes over context-free prefills too, in place of the ASM FP8 prefill (`mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd`). The metadata builder stops building ASM PS metadata when this backend is selected, and `AiterMLAImpl.forward_mha` then falls back to the common path.

Support is checked through the standard prefill-backend hooks. vLLM does not hard-code any shape or model:
- `supported_dtypes = [bf16]`, because the kernel writes BF16 output;
- `supports_compute_capability` requires gfx950;
- `is_available` requires AITER and the FlyDSL FP8 API;
- `validate_configuration` defers to AITER's `flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_supported` for the head dims.

An explicit selection that fails these checks raises at startup. At runtime, inputs the kernel cannot take (empty, or ≥2³¹ elements) use the parent's BF16 path.

`vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_per_tensor_fp8_quant.py` is a small Triton kernel adapted from ATOM#2191's fused QKV quantizer (MIT). It quantizes up to three strided `[tokens, heads, dim]` tensors in two launches, each with its own amax/descale. V is quantized directly from its strided view of the `kv_b_proj` output. Compile-time specialization does not depend on token counts (only the grid size does), so varying batch shapes do not recompile, and no atomics are used. Unlike ATOM's KV quantizer, element counts are runtime arguments.

**Why not reuse `ops.scaled_fp8_quant`.** vLLM's dynamic per-tensor quantizer (`dynamic_scaled_fp8_quant`, also behind `QuantFP8`) gives the same result: descales within 1e-6 relative, values within 1 e4m3 ulp. It is too slow for this path, for three reasons:
- It takes one 2D tensor per call, so Q/K/V need three calls (memset, amax, quant each).
- The strided V (row stride 256) takes its per-row path: one 256-thread block and one `atomicMax` per 128-element row, i.e. T×H rows.
- An all-zero input gets descale 0. ATOM uses a positive descale in that case to avoid FMHA NaNs, and this kernel does the same.

`rocm_aiter_ops.per_tensor_quant` returns wrong results for the strided V. GPU time on MI355X, 12 heads, q/k 192 and v 128 (v a strided view):

| Tokens | This kernel (Q/K/V, one call) | `scaled_fp8_quant` ×3 | `scaled_fp8_quant` ×3, V made contiguous first |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 50 µs | 189 µs | 59 µs |
| 8,192 | 50 µs | 1,318 µs | 237 µs |
| 65,536 | 352 µs | 10,165 µs | 1,306 µs |

At 65,536 tokens, V alone takes 9,284 µs with `scaled_fp8_quant` and 110 µs here. The existing op is faster only for a single small contiguous tensor (Q alone at 1,024 tokens: 21 µs vs 44 µs), which this path never quantizes.

**AITER requirement.** This needs an AITER build containing:
- ROCm/aiter#5718 (`flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_supported`)
- ROCm/aiter#5508 (short-query split-K)
- ROCm/aiter#5405 (`softmax_scale` in `flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_func`)

All three are already on AITER main. #5718 is the newest of them, so a build that has the capability check also has the other two. #5508 only affects performance. The current `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly (AITER 0.1.22.post1) predates them, so there this backend reports itself unavailable.

**AOT build.** ROCm/aiter#5796 and #5901 pre-compile the FlyDSL FP8 FMHA for Kimi-K3 TP8 (`12:12:192:128`, `varlen_cross` layout, 92 kernels) during AITER source builds, so serving no longer JIT-compiles them. The new-token call therefore passes `cross_seqlen=True`, as ATOM does.
- With `cross_seqlen=False`, the new-token call would use the `varlen` layout, which is not pre-compiled.
- For equal q/kv lengths, the two layouts give bit-identical output and LSE. Checked 8 batch shapes.
- Kernel time with `cross_seqlen=True` is within ±2% for most shapes and 7% faster for 1×8192. Batches of several equal-length sequences are slower: 4×2048 +15 µs, 8×1024 +4 µs.

Coverage check: the 92 AOT kernels (built with `aiter.aot.flydsl.fmha_fp8` from AITER main) were put into an empty `FLYDSL_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR`, and `FLYDSL_RUNTIME_RUN_ONLY=1` was set, which makes any cache miss raise.
- Through this backend, all 12 new-token and context-chunk calls were served from the AOT cache, and the cache did not grow. The calls covered 1–32 sequences, 17–8192 new tokens and contexts of 0–131072 tokens.
- With `cross_seqlen=False`, all 20 new-token calls missed.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs for FlyDSL/FP8 MLA prefill:
- #51551 (draft) adds a gfx942-only FP8 context-prefill path for 12-head Kimi-K3. It uses AITER's Gluon kernel (ROCm/aiter#4645) with static, offline-calibrated per-head scales. This PR targets gfx950 through FlyDSL, uses dynamic per-tensor scales with no calibration artifact, and also covers new tokens and context-free prefills.
- #53335 is a non-MLA FlyDSL BF16 attention backend.
- #58887 fixes an ASM PS-metadata race. It is orthogonal: that path is skipped while this backend is selected. Both PRs touch the `_fp8_prefill_enabled` gate in `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder.__init__`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to implement this change and to run the tests and benchmarks below.

## Test Plan

**Unit tests** (MI355X, gfx950):
```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k ROCM_AITER
python -m pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_flydsl_fp8_prefill.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_selector.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
python tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12 <changed vllm files>
```
`ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8` is added to `PREFILL_BACKENDS_TO_TEST` in `test_mla_backends.py`, so `test_backend_correctness` and `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` check it against the SDPA reference.
- GLM dims (v=256) are skipped at collection through `validate_configuration`.
- For this backend only, the tolerance is `rtol=2**-4, atol=0.3`. With per-tensor e4m3 Q/K/V, a row that attends to a few tokens is off by up to about 2⁻⁴·max|V|. The largest observed diff was about 0.25.
- A new `context_free_prefill` spec, run for this backend, covers the builder change that keeps `ROCM_AITER_MLA`'s ASM FP8 prefill from bypassing the selected prefill backend.

The registry and selector tests cover registration, bf16-only, gfx950 gating, availability, and deferring to AITER's check. The backend test file covers:
- the quant kernel against a torch reference: at most 1 e4m3 ulp, with strided V, empty and all-zero inputs;
- the backend's FP8 new-token and context-chunk outputs against its BF16 path, including short-q/long-kv chunks and sequences with empty context;
- FP8 Q reuse by the context chunk;
- `validate_configuration` rejecting a head dim that AITER does not support.

**End-to-end.** The server config is the InferenceX Kimi-K3 MI355X job (`kimik3_fp4_mi355x_mtp.sh`, conc 48, no spec decode). A/B differs only in the MLA prefill backend, and both runs use the same AITER build. The end-to-end numbers were measured with the first revision of this PR, which enabled the same code path through an env flag inside `ROCM_AITER_FA`. Apart from `cross_seqlen=True` (bit-identical outputs), the kernel calls are unchanged.

```bash
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --language-model-only --moe-backend auto --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL","max_cudagraph_capture_size":96,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"],"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[2,...,96]}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":224875000000,"lazy_offload":false}}'
# env: VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1
#      AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 AITER_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4

# FP8 arm: --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}'
```

- **Accuracy:**
  - lm-eval `gsm8k`, 5-shot, full 1319, via `local-completions`, `num_concurrent=64`, temperature 0.
  - InferenceX `kimi_tool_call_schema_full` (Kimi Vendor Verifier, 408 records, the CI eval for this job), run twice per arm.
- **Performance:**
  - InferenceX agentic replay: `aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp --concurrency 48 --benchmark-duration 3600 --warmup-grace-period 1800 --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126 ...`, the same command and aiperf commit as CI. One run per arm.
  - Prefill TTFT: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-output-len 1 --ignore-eos` at 8K, 32K, 128K and 64K-with-56K-shared-prefix inputs. A warmup pass runs first, and each arm is run twice.

## Test Result

**Unit tests** (MI355X, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`):
- `test_mla_backends.py -k ROCM_AITER`: 869 passed, 296 skipped. Three `ROCM_AITER_FA` cases (fp8 KV, scales 2/3, TP4) failed with CUDA OOM because another job had filled the shared GPU. All three pass when rerun individually, both on this branch and on `main`.
- All 290 `ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8` cases pass; the GLM-dim cases are skipped.
- Backend, selector and registry tests: 48 passed.
- `pre-commit` passes on the changed files. `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12` reports `Success: no issues found in 7 source files`.

**Accuracy (8×MI355X, TP8/DCP8):**

| Eval | Baseline | FlyDSL FP8 |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K 5-shot strict-match / flexible-extract | 0.9621 / 0.9621 | 0.9621 / 0.9621 |
| kimi_tool_call_schema_full, run 1 / run 2 | 0.9779 / 0.9877 | 0.9755 / 0.9951 |

The tool-call eval varies by about 2 points between runs of the same server. The two arms are within that noise.

**Agentic replay (InferenceX agentx-mvp, conc 48, 3600 s):**

| Metric | Baseline | FlyDSL FP8 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT p50 / p90 / p99 (ms) | 1176 / 3690 / 22443 | 1119 / 3106 / 16155 | -4.8% / -15.8% / -28.0% |
| ITL p50 / p90 / p99 (ms) | 51.1 / 74.6 / 188.0 | 49.2 / 68.2 / 130.5 | -3.8% / -8.7% / -30.6% |
| P90 interactivity (1000 / ITL p90, tok/s) | 13.40 | 14.67 | +9.5% |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 91,787 | 95,931 | +4.5% |
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 609.2 | 638.5 | +4.8% |
| Completed / errored requests | 2653 / 8 | 2744 / 6 | |

The errors are client-side aiperf `InvalidInferenceResultError`/`ClientOSError` records and appear in both arms. Neither server logged any errors. This workload has very long inputs (ISL p50 about 86K) and about 97% prefix-cache hits. Most prefill work is therefore short new-token segments against long cached context, which is where the FP8 kernel gains most. Shorter prefills also shorten the stalls of decodes batched with them, which lowers the ITL tail.

**Prefill TTFT (`vllm bench serve`, output_len 1, mean of 2 runs):**

| Case | Baseline mean TTFT | FlyDSL FP8 mean TTFT | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K fresh prefill ×128, c16 | 6676 ms | 6659 ms | -0.2% |
| 32K (chunked, with context) ×32, c4 | 5528 ms | 5441 ms | -1.6% |
| 128K ×8, c2 | 13252 ms | 12283 ms | -7.3% |
| 64K with a 56K shared cached prefix ×32, c4 | 5071 ms\* | 4758 ms | -6.2% |

\* Baseline run 2 only. Run 1 overlapped another client's load on the same server and was discarded.

**Backend micro-benchmark** (one GPU, 12 heads, qk 192 / v 128; FP8 times include quantization). The "context" rows time the new-token call plus one context-chunk call, with Q quantized once and reused, as in `forward_mha`:

| Shape | BF16 `flash_attn_varlen_func` | FlyDSL FP8 | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| new tokens 1×8192, causal | 313 µs | 229 µs | 1.37× |
| new q 8192 + context kv 64K | 3821 µs | 2469 µs | 1.55× |
| new q 1024 + context kv 64K | 1278 µs | 549 µs | 2.33× |
| new q 128 + context kv 64K | 1251 µs | 351 µs | 3.56× |

Short new-token-only calls (≤2K tokens) carry about 50 µs of host-side launch overhead from the quantizer. This did not show up end-to-end; the 8K fresh-prefill case is flat.

**JIT.** With an AITER build that includes the AOT kernels (#5796/#5901), the FlyDSL FMHA is not JIT-compiled while serving. Without them, each new FMHA configuration compiles on first use (about 1 s) and is then cached on disk. The Triton quantizer compiles 3 variants (Q/K/V, K/V, Q) once, which Triton caches.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8 MLA prefill backend.
+
+Checks the fused per-tensor FP8 quantization against a torch reference, and the
+backend's FP8 new-token and context-chunk attention (including long contexts
+and Q reuse) against the BF16 ROCM_AITER_FA backend. End-to-end correctness
+against SDPA is covered in tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py.
+"""
+
+import math
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+    pytest.skip("ROCm-only test", allow_module_level=True)
+
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.prefill import aiter_flydsl_fp8  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.prefill.aiter_flash_attn import (  # noqa: E402
+    AiterFlashAttnPrefillBackend,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.prefill.aiter_flydsl_fp8 import (  # noqa: E402
+    AiterFlyDSLFP8PrefillBackend,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.prefill.base import MLADimensions  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.prefill.selector import (  # noqa: E402
+    MLAPrefillSelectorConfig,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_per_tensor_fp8_quant import (  # noqa: E402
+    _BLOCK,
+    _PARTS,
+    fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant,
+)
+
+NUM_HEADS = 12
+QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM = 128
+QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM = 64
+V_HEAD_DIM = 128
+KV_LORA_RANK = 512
+QK_HEAD_DIM = QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM + QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM
+FP8_DTYPE = torch.float8_e4m3fn
+
+
+def _reference_quant(x: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    amax = x.abs().float().max() if x.numel() else x.new_zeros((), dtype=torch.float)
+    descale = amax / torch.finfo(FP8_DTYPE).max if amax > 0 else amax.new_tensor(1e-6)
+    x_fp8 = (x.float() / descale).clamp(-448, 448).to(FP8_DTYPE)
+    return x_fp8, descale.reshape(1)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [0, 1, 37, 8192])
+def test_fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant_matches_reference(num_tokens: int) -> None:
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    q = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda") * 4
+    k = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda")
+    kv = torch.randn(
+        num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM + V_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda"
+    )
+    # V is a strided view of the kv_b_proj output, as in MLA prefill.
+    v = kv[..., QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM:]
+    inputs = [x.to(torch.bfloat16) for x in (q, k, v)]
+    outputs, descales = fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant(*inputs)
+    for x, x_fp8, descale in zip(inputs, outputs, descales):
+        ref_fp8, ref_descale = _reference_quant(x)
+        assert x_fp8.shape == x.shape and x_fp8.is_contiguous()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(descale, ref_descale, rtol=1e-6, atol=0)
+        # x * (1 / descale) may round one e4m3 step away from x / descale.
+        ulp_diff = x_fp8.view(torch.int8).int() - ref_fp8.view(torch.int8).int()
+        assert ulp_diff.numel() == 0 or ulp_diff.abs().max() <= 1
+
+
+_STRIPE = _PARTS * _BLOCK
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "numel",
+    [1, _BLOCK, _BLOCK + 1, _STRIPE - 1, _STRIPE, _STRIPE + 1, 3 * _STRIPE + 7],
+)
+def test_fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant_covers_every_element(numel: int) -> None:
+    """One grid serves inputs of different sizes; no element may be dropped."""
+    x = torch.full((numel, 1, 1), 0.5, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    expected = 100.0 / torch.finfo(FP8_DTYPE).max
+    for pos in sorted({0, _BLOCK - 1, _BLOCK, _STRIPE - 1, _STRIPE, numel - 1}):
+        if pos >= numel:
+            continue
+        probe = x.clone()
+        probe[pos] = 100.0
+        _, (descale,) = fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant(probe)
+        assert descale.item() == pytest.approx(expected), f"missed element {pos}"
+
+
+def test_fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant_zero_input() -> None:
+    x = torch.zeros(4, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    (x_fp8,), (descale,) = fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant(x)
+    assert descale.item() > 0
+    assert x_fp8.float().abs().max().item() == 0
+
+
+def _make_backend(backend_cls, v_head_dim: int = V_HEAD_DIM):
+    vllm_config = SimpleNamespace(model_config=SimpleNamespace(dtype=torch.bfloat16))
+    return backend_cls(
+        num_heads=NUM_HEADS,
+        scale=1.0 / math.sqrt(QK_HEAD_DIM),
+        kv_lora_rank=KV_LORA_RANK,
+        qk_nope_head_dim=QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM,
+        qk_rope_head_dim=QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM,
+        v_head_dim=v_head_dim,
+        vllm_config=vllm_config,
+    )
+
+
+def _selector_config(v_head_dim: int) -> MLAPrefillSelectorConfig:
+    return MLAPrefillSelectorConfig(
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        mla_dimensions=MLADimensions(
+            qk_nope_head_dim=QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM,
+            qk_rope_head_dim=QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM,
+            v_head_dim=v_head_dim,
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def _skip_if_unsupported() -> None:
+    reasons = AiterFlyDSLFP8PrefillBackend.validate_configuration(
+        current_platform.get_device_capability(), _selector_config(V_HEAD_DIM)
+    )
+    if reasons:
+        pytest.skip(f"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8 unavailable: {reasons}")
+
+
+def _cu_seqlens(lens: list[int]) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.tensor([0, *torch.tensor(lens).cumsum(0).tolist()]).to(
+        device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+
+
+def _assert_close_to_bf16(fp8_result, bf16_result) -> None:
+    fp8_out, fp8_lse = fp8_result
+    bf16_out, bf16_lse = bf16_result
+    assert fp8_out.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    assert fp8_out.shape == bf16_out.shape and fp8_lse.shape == bf16_lse.shape
+    cos = F.cosine_similarity(
+        fp8_out.float().flatten(), bf16_out.float().flatten(), dim=0
+    )
+    assert cos > 0.998
+    # FP8 rounding of Q.K dominates rows that attend to only a few keys.
+    lse_err = (fp8_lse - bf16_lse).abs()
+    assert lse_err.max() < 0.25 and lse_err.mean() < 0.01
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "query_lens,context_lens",
+    [([2048], [16384]), ([128], [65536]), ([300, 1, 4000], [0, 5000, 64])],
+)
+def test_flydsl_fp8_prefill_matches_bf16(monkeypatch, query_lens, context_lens):
+    _skip_if_unsupported()
+    fp8_backend = _make_backend(AiterFlyDSLFP8PrefillBackend)
+    bf16_backend = _make_backend(AiterFlashAttnPrefillBackend)
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    num_tokens, num_ctx = sum(query_lens), sum(context_lens)
+    q = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+    k = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+    v = torch.randn(
+        num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM + V_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda"
+    ).bfloat16()[..., QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM:]
+    ctx_k = torch.randn(num_ctx, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+    ctx_v = torch.randn(num_ctx, NUM_HEADS, V_HEAD_DIM, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+
+    metadata = SimpleNamespace(
+        query_start_loc=_cu_seqlens(query_lens), max_query_len=max(query_lens)
+    )
+    chunk = SimpleNamespace(
+        token_slice=slice(0, num_tokens),
+        query_start_loc=_cu_seqlens(query_lens),
+        cu_seq_lens=_cu_seqlens(context_lens),
+        max_query_len=max(query_lens),
+        max_seq_len=max(context_lens),
+    )
+    quantized_counts: list[int] = []
+
+    def spy_quant(*tensors, **kwargs):
+        quantized_counts.append(len(tensors))
+        return fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant(*tensors, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(aiter_flydsl_fp8, "fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant", spy_quant)
+    results = []
+    for backend in (fp8_backend, bf16_backend):
+        backend.prepare_metadata(metadata)
+        new = backend.run_prefill_new_tokens(q, k, v, return_softmax_lse=True)
+        ctx = backend.run_prefill_context_chunk(
+            chunk, q[chunk.token_slice], ctx_k, ctx_v

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Fused dynamic per-tensor FP8 quantization of up to three attention inputs.
+
+Each ``[tokens, heads, dim]`` input (possibly strided, e.g. V as a view of the
+``kv_b_proj`` output) gets its own amax and FP32 descale. A partial-amax pass
+and a reduce-and-quantize pass cover all inputs in two launches; the kernel
+boundary is the only global barrier, so no atomics or zero-initialization are
+needed and the ops are CUDA-graph safe. Compile-time specialization does not
+depend on the token counts (only the grid size does), so varying batch shapes
+do not recompile.
+
+One grid covers all the inputs in each launch, so a program can land past the
+end of a smaller input. Such programs do no work and compute no address, and
+every load and store is masked regardless, so no out-of-range pointer is formed
+or dereferenced.
+
+Adapted from the fused QKV quantizer in ROCm/ATOM (atom/model_ops/
+triton_fused_qkv_quant.py, MIT license).
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+_BLOCK = 4096
+_PARTS = 256
+# Descale for all-zero or empty inputs. A positive value keeps downstream
+# attention kernels from producing NaNs.
+_MIN_DESCALE = 1e-6
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _load(X, offsets, N, SHAPE: tl.constexpr, STRIDE: tl.constexpr):
+    heads, dim = SHAPE
+    offsets = offsets.to(tl.int64)
+    physical = (
+        offsets // (heads * dim) * STRIDE[0]
+        + offsets // dim % heads * STRIDE[1]
+        + offsets % dim * STRIDE[2]
+    )
+    return tl.load(X + physical, offsets < N, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _partial_amax(
+    X,
+    Partial,
+    N,
+    SHAPE: tl.constexpr,
+    STRIDE: tl.constexpr,
+    PARTS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    # The grid is fixed at PARTS, so the trip count is per-program: it drops to
+    # zero once this program's stripe starts past the end of this input.
+    start = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK
+    acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), tl.float32)
+    for step in range(tl.cdiv(N - start, PARTS * BLOCK)):
+        offsets = start + step * PARTS * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+        x = _load(X, offsets, N, SHAPE, STRIDE)
+        acc = tl.maximum(acc, tl.abs(x))
+    tl.store(Partial + tl.program_id(0), tl.max(acc, 0))
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _fused_amax_kernel(
+    X0,
+    X1,
+    X2,
+    Partial,
+    N0,
+    N1,
+    N2,
+    SHAPES: tl.constexpr,
+    STRIDES: tl.constexpr,
+    PARTS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    idx = tl.program_id(1)
+    if idx == 0:
+        _partial_amax(X0, Partial, N0, SHAPES[0], STRIDES[0], PARTS, BLOCK)
+    elif idx == 1:
+        _partial_amax(X1, Partial + PARTS, N1, SHAPES[1], STRIDES[1], PARTS, BLOCK)
+    else:
+        _partial_amax(X2, Partial + 2 * PARTS, N2, SHAPES[2], STRIDES[2], PARTS, BLOCK)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _quant(
+    X,
+    Y,
+    Partial,
+    Scale,
+    N,
+    SHAPE: tl.constexpr,
+    STRIDE: tl.constexpr,
+    PARTS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    FP8_MAX: tl.constexpr,
+    MIN_DESCALE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    # One grid covers all inputs, so it is sized for the largest. Programs
+    # past this input's end do nothing; program 0 still writes the descale,
+    # which is what an empty input needs.
+    start = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK
+    if start < N or start == 0:
+        offsets = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+        x = _load(X, offsets, N, SHAPE, STRIDE)
+        amax = tl.max(tl.load(Partial + tl.arange(0, PARTS)), 0)
+        descale = amax / FP8_MAX
+        descale = tl.where(descale > 0, descale, MIN_DESCALE)
+        y = tl.clamp(x * (1.0 / descale), -FP8_MAX, FP8_MAX)
+        tl.store(Y + offsets, y.to(Y.dtype.element_ty), offsets < N)
+        if start == 0:
+            tl.store(Scale, descale)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _fused_quant_kernel(
+    X0,
+    X1,
+    X2,
+    Y0,
+    Y1,
+    Y2,
+    Partial,
+    Scales,
+    N0,
+    N1,
+    N2,
+    SHAPES: tl.constexpr,
+    STRIDES: tl.constexpr,
+    PARTS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    FP8_MAX: tl.constexpr,
+    MIN_DESCALE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    idx = tl.program_id(1)
+    if idx == 0:
+        _quant(
+            X0,
+            Y0,
+            Partial,
+            Scales,
+            N0,
+            SHAPES[0],
+            STRIDES[0],
+            PARTS,
+            BLOCK,
+            FP8_MAX,
+            MIN_DESCALE,
+        )
+    elif idx == 1:
+        _quant(
+            X1,
+            Y1,
+            Partial + PARTS,
+            Scales + 1,
+            N1,
+            SHAPES[1],
+            STRIDES[1],
+            PARTS,
+            BLOCK,
+            FP8_MAX,
+            MIN_DESCALE,
+        )
+    else:
+        _quant(
+            X2,
+            Y2,
+            Partial + 2 * PARTS,
+            Scales + 2,
+            N2,
+            SHAPES[2],
+            STRIDES[2],
+            PARTS,
+            BLOCK,
+            FP8_MAX,
+            MIN_DESCALE,
+        )
+
+
+def fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant(
+    *tensors: torch.Tensor,
+    fp8_dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float8_e4m3fn,
+) -> tuple[tuple[torch.Tensor, ...], tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]]:
+    """Quantize each input to FP8 with its own dynamic per-tensor scale.
+
+    Args:
+        tensors: One to three BF16/FP16 ``[tokens, heads, dim]`` tensors on the
+            same device. Arbitrary strides are supported; token counts may
+            differ and may be zero.
+        fp8_dtype: The FP8 output dtype.
+
+    Returns:
+        ``(outputs, descales)``: contiguous FP8 tensors with the input shapes
+        and FP32 shape-``[1]`` descales (``amax / fp8_max``, or 1e-6 for
+        all-zero or empty inputs).
+
+    """
+    if not 1 <= len(tensors) <= 3:
+        raise ValueError(f"Expected 1 to 3 tensors, got {len(tensors)}")
+    first = tensors[0]
+    for x in tensors:
+        if x.ndim != 3 or x.shape[1] == 0 or x.shape[2] == 0:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Expected [tokens, nonzero heads, nonzero dim], got {x.shape}"
+            )
+        if x.device != first.device or x.dtype not in (
+            torch.bfloat16,
+            torch.float16,
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Inputs must be BF16/FP16 tensors on the same device")
+
+    outputs = tuple(
+        torch.empty(x.shape, dtype=fp8_dtype, device=x.device) for x in tensors
+    )
+    scales = torch.empty(len(tensors), dtype=torch.float32, device=first.device)
+    numels = [x.numel() for x in tensors]
+    partial = torch.empty(
+        (len(tensors), _PARTS), dtype=torch.float32, device=first.device
+    )
+
+    # Unused slots alias the first tensor; their programs never run.
+    pad = 3 - len(tensors)
+    xs = (*tensors, *(first,) * pad)
+    ys = (*outputs, *(outputs[0],) * pad)
+    ns = (*numels, *(0,) * pad)
+    shapes = tuple(tuple(x.shape[1:]) for x in xs)
+    strides = tuple(x.stride() for x in xs)
+
+    _fused_amax_kernel[(_PARTS, len(tensors))](
+        *xs, partial, *ns, shapes, strides, _PARTS, _BLOCK, num_warps=4
+    )
+    _fused_quant_kernel[(max(1, triton.cdiv(max(numels), _BLOCK)), len(tensors))](
+        *xs,
+        *ys,
+        partial,
+        scales,
+        *ns,
+        shapes,
+        strides,
+        _PARTS,
+        _BLOCK,
+        torch.finfo(fp8_dtype).max,
+        _MIN_DESCALE,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+    return outputs, tuple(scales[i : i + 1] for i in range(len(tensors)))

inline_comments.body: **Question**: what's the rationale behind implementing this here rather than re-using an existing quant kernel?
**Question**: does this work even though this backend does not supports_out?

I compared against the existing kernels first. On MI355X, with 12 heads, q/k 192 and v 128, and V a strided view of the `kv_b_proj` output:
- `rocm_aiter_ops.per_tensor_quant` returns wrong results for the strided V.
- `ops.scaled_fp8_quant` matches this kernel: descales within 1e-6, values within 1 e4m3 ulp. It is much slower here, though:

| Tokens | This kernel (Q/K/V, one call) | `scaled_fp8_quant` ×3 | ×3, V made contiguous first |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 50 µs | 189 µs | 59 µs |
| 8,192 | 50 µs | 1,318 µs | 237 µs |
| 65,536 | 352 µs | 10,165 µs | 1,306 µs |

Why it is slower:
- It takes one 2D tensor per call, so Q/K/V need 3 × (memset + amax + quant).
- V's row stride sends it down the per-row path: one 256-thread block and one `atomicMax` per 128-element row, and there are T×H rows. At 65K tokens, V alone takes 9.3 ms there versus 110 µs here.
- An all-zero input gets descale 0.

This kernel is adapted from ATOM's fused QKV quantizer. The one change is that token counts are runtime args, so varying batch shapes don't recompile.

I'd be happy to move it somewhere more general, or to fix the strided path of `dynamic_scaled_fp8_quant` in a follow-up, if you prefer.

Yes. `forward_mha` passes `out` only together with `output_scale`, i.e. fused quantized output. That requires `supports_quant_output()`, which this backend doesn't claim (neither does `ROCM_AITER_FA`), so `out` is always `None` here and FlyDSL allocates the output itself.

If a caller did pass `out`, FlyDSL would write into it: it validates a contiguous BF16 `[T, H, Dv]` buffer.

I kept `supports_out()` False because nothing on the ROCm MLA path consumes it yet; only the Kimi-K3 NVIDIA module does. The context-chunk path asserts `out is None`.

Saving the extra `output.copy_` for context-free prefills could be a follow-up with numbers.

hi @simondanielsson , thanks for your review! Here are the updates regarding your concerns:
1. **Standalone backend.** The FlyDSL FP8 path now lives in its own prefill backend, `ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/aiter_flydsl_fp8.py`). It subclasses `AiterFlashAttnPrefillBackend`, so the few inputs FlyDSL can't take fall back to the parent's BF16 path. `ROCM_AITER_FA` is back to its `main` version.
   - Select it with `--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}'`. The env var is gone.

     - `supported_dtypes = [bf16]`.
     - `supports_compute_capability` requires gfx950.
     - `is_available` requires AITER and the FlyDSL FP8 API.
     - `validate_configuration` defers to AITER's `flydsl_flash_attn_fp8_supported` for the head dims.
   - An explicit but unsupported selection therefore fails at startup, instead of silently running BF16 as before.
   - The backend is not in the ROCm auto-selection priorities.
2. **Correctness tests.** The backend is added to `PREFILL_BACKENDS_TO_TEST` in `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py`, so `test_backend_correctness` and `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` run it against the SDPA reference.
   - GLM dims (v=256) are skipped at collection through `validate_configuration`.
   - The tolerance is loosened for this backend only: `rtol=2**-4, atol=0.3`. With per-tensor e4m3 Q/K/V, a row that attends to only a few tokens is off by up to about 2⁻⁴·max|V|. The largest observed diff was about 0.25.
   - I also added a `context_free_prefill` spec to `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness`, which this backend runs. It covers the builder change that stops `ROCM_AITER_MLA`'s ASM FP8 prefill from bypassing the selected prefill backend.
   - Registry and selector unit tests are added as well.
   - Result on MI355X with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k ROCM_AITER` → 869 passed and 296 skipped. Three `ROCM_AITER_FA` cases hit CUDA OOM because another job filled the shared GPU; all three pass individually on this branch and on `main`. All `ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8` cases pass.
3. **Default for FP8 KV.** Agreed, this should stay opt-in until there is a broader sweep. It also overlaps with your #44544 (`ROCM_AITER_ASM` as the gfx950 default for FP8 KV). I think the two can coexist as separate backends:
   - `ROCM_AITER_ASM` consumes the FP8 KV cache directly.
   - This one quantizes the BF16 Q/K/V dynamically per tensor, so it doesn't depend on the KV cache dtype.

   If it helps decide the default, I can run a same-image sweep of FA, ASM and FlyDSL-FP8 (ISL 1k/8k/32k+, concurrency 8–256, plus the Kimi-K3 agentic replay) once #44544 is rebased.

Three technical suggestions:

1. The quantizer grid uses the largest tensor size. V is smaller, so masked threads can still form out-of-range pointers. Please clamp indices or use separate grids.

2. The quantizer allocates temporary buffers on every call. Reusing fixed buffers could reduce the ~50 µs overhead for short inputs.

3. Please disable the ASM FP8 prefill path directly when this backend is selected, instead of relying only on missing metadata to bypass it.

Keeping this opt-in makes sense: short prefills show little benefit, while FP8 accuracy needs a wider long-context evaluation.

@ChuanLi1101 Thanks for the careful read — points 1 and 3 are fixed in 19a77e3, and I have numbers for point 2.

**1. Out-of-range pointers in the shared quant grid**

You're right that the grid is sized for the largest input, so programs can land past the end of a smaller one. Every load and store was already masked and the offset math is int64, so nothing was dereferenced or wrapped — but those programs still computed addresses they had no business computing. Both kernels now stop before that:

- `_partial_amax` derives its trip count per program, `tl.cdiv(N - start, PARTS * BLOCK)`, which is 0 once the program's stripe starts past the end of this input. It still stores its (zero) partial, which the reduce needs.
- `_quant` guards the body with `if start < N or start == 0`. Program 0 stays alive unconditionally so an empty input still gets its descale written.

I added `test_fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant_covers_every_element` to the kernel test: it plants the global max at `{0, BLOCK-1, BLOCK, STRIPE-1, STRIPE, numel-1}` for sizes straddling the 4096-element block and 1048576-element stripe boundaries, up to 3,145,735 elements. It fails if a single element is dropped (verified by shrinking the amax loop to one stripe). The change is perf-neutral: host 46.3–46.8 µs, e2e 349.2 µs at 65K tokens, same as before.

**2. Per-call temporary buffers**

I measured this on MI355X before changing it, since the buffers are tiny (`partial` is 3×256 f32, `scales` is 3 f32). Host cost of `fused_per_tensor_fp8_quant(q, k, v)`:

| Variant | Host | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|
| current (5 allocations) | 46.6 µs | — |
| reuse `partial` only | 44.2 µs | −2.4 µs |
| reuse `partial` + `scales` | 42.7 µs | −3.9 µs |
| one merged scratch allocation | 46.7 µs | +0.1 µs |

Where the 46.6 µs goes: 28 µs is the two Triton launches (an empty kernel with the same signature already costs 15.2 µs), 10.2 µs is `torch.empty` ×5, and the rest is the Python wrapper. So the ceiling on reuse is ~8% of host cost and ~1% of the 349 µs e2e at 65K tokens. The three FP8 outputs can't be reused at all — they are returned and stay live for the whole attention call.

Reusing `scales` specifically has a correctness trap: the backend keeps `self._q_fp8 = (q, q_fp8, q_descale)` across the forward, where `q_descale` is a view into that call's `scales`, and each context chunk then calls the quantizer again for its own K/V. A shared per-instance `scales` would be overwritten under the still-live `q_descale` unless keyed by tensor count — exactly the kind of implicit invariant that breaks later.

Given ~2 µs for the only unambiguously safe part (`partial`, which never escapes the function) against making a pure function stateful, I left it as is. Happy to add the `partial` cache if you'd still prefer it — it's a five-line change.

**3. Disabling the ASM FP8 prefill directly**

Agreed, keying off absent PS metadata was too indirect. There's now a single predicate in `rocm_aiter_mla.py`:

```python
def _asm_fp8_prefill_superseded(prefill_backend: object) -> bool:
    return isinstance(prefill_backend, AiterFlyDSLFP8PrefillBackend)
```

used in both places so they can't drift:

- `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder.__init__` folds it into `_fp8_prefill_enabled`, so the PS workspace buffers aren't allocated either.
- `AiterMLAImpl.forward_mha` checks the actual `prefill_metadata.prefill_backend` instance and defers to the parent, instead of inferring it from `fp8_prefill_qo_indptr is None`.

`test_mla_backends.py::test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` covers this through the `context_free_prefill` spec.

**4. Opt-in**

Agreed — it stays out of the ROCm auto-selection priorities and is only reachable via `--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8"}'`.
